title: Recognize Safety Hold Agreements
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill allows licensed firearms dealers to store firearms temporarily for owners who request it (called a 'safety hold agreement') at no charge. It provides liability protection for dealers against lawsuits related to these agreements, except in cases of negligent storage or unlawful conduct. The bill also keeps these agreements confidential and allows dealers to dispose of firearms if owners don't reclaim them.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill helps prevent harm by allowing people to voluntarily place their firearms in temporary storage during crisis situations—such as when someone is experiencing suicidal thoughts or emotional distress—without legal risk to gun dealers. They contend the liability protection encourages dealers to participate in these voluntary safety measures, potentially saving lives while respecting property rights since owners can reclaim their firearms at any time.
aiConArguments: Opponents worry that broad liability immunity could discourage dealers from taking reasonable precautions with stored firearms, potentially creating safety risks. Some also express concern about the confidentiality provision, arguing it limits transparency and oversight of these agreements, and question whether the bill adequately protects against dealers selling firearms that owners intended to reclaim or against dealers storing firearms from prohibited individuals.
